equity_bridge.item: Redeemable noncontrolling interests (temporary equity, at redemption value)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (4.5-5.5% total, ~3.5-4% internal) cross-checked against the 5-year revenue CAGR of 5.4% (FY2020 was the COVID trough, so that overstates trend). Equity CAGR is negative and unusable as a growth anchor: cumulative buybacks ($2.37B FY2021-25) exceed retained earnings.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.4% 5y, -1.6% 3y) diverges from revenue (5.4% / 1.4%) and EPS (3.1% / -5.9%) by far more than 30%: book value is shrinking because of buybacks, not because the business is; EPS 3-year CAGR is negative because FY2022 was the post-COVID PPE peak and FY2023-24 carried the cyber incident.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes): FY2020 527 (550-8.8-14), FY2022 420 (506-54-32), FY2025 519 (573-39-15). The owner-FCF 5-year CAGR (-0.3%) is below the reported-FCF CAGR (0.8%) because equity-award taxes were unusually low in FY2020; on a 3-year view owner FCF grew faster than reported (7.3% vs 4.2%) as SBC fell from $54M to $39M. FY2020 FCF ($550M) was flattered by PPE demand; FY2023 ($353M) was depressed by the cyber incident.

scenario_narratives.base: Henry Schein is a 3-4% organic grower whose earnings story is margin repair rather than top line: the October 2023 cyber incident, a heavy restructuring cadence and post-COVID PPE normalisation took the GAAP EBITDA margin from 8.6% (FY2021) to 7.0-7.3%; the base case assumes the KKR-backed value-creation plan recovers roughly a third of that gap by FY2029 and that FY2026 lands at the raised guidance midpoint. Cash generation is steady but leverage (~3x net debt/EBITDA including bank lines) and $1.6B of NCI claims mean the equity is a levered claim on a modest-margin distributor.
scenario_narratives.bull: Specialty products and Henry Schein One carry group growth to ~5% while the distribution business regains share; the value-creation programme delivers fully, restructuring stops recurring, and the group earns its adjusted-EBITDA margin on a GAAP basis. The buyback keeps compounding per-share value and the market re-rates toward the 18x terminal multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Dental demand stays soft and consumables commoditise under online and direct-channel competition, so organic growth stalls at ~1.5% and the margin drifts to 7.0% despite continuing restructuring spend. With ~$3.3B net debt and $906M of redeemable NCI puts ahead of common equity, a modest operating disappointment is amplified at the per-share level.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC and equity-award taxes expensed, share count held flat (funded by an $850M FY2025 buyback), consolidated flows with NCI deducted once in the bridge at balance-sheet value, and a GAAP (not adjusted) EBITDA basis because restructuring has recurred every year since 2022. The value hinges on whether the margin recovers, not on growth; the terminal multiple is capped at 14-18x because a 3% grower does not earn a compounder's exit.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: total debt $3.46B including $1.02B of bank credit lines; net debt/GAAP EBITDA ~3.3x. A 100bp move in WACC is worth a large share of the equity value.

NCI: $906M redeemable NCI is carried at redemption value and $660M permanent NCI at book; if the economic value of the minorities' stakes (notably in Henry Schein One) exceeds book, the deduction is understated.
Margin thesis: the base case needs ~90bp of pre-SBC EBITDA margin recovery from the value-creation plan; FY2021-25 margins went the other way.
Acquisitions: ~$200M/yr of tuck-in spend is excluded from both growth and flows; if management keeps buying growth, either the growth path is too low or the flows are too high.
Dental end-market cyclicality and channel disintermediation (online, direct-from-manufacturer, DSO purchasing power).
Cyber / IT: the October 2023 incident cost roughly a year of margin; a repeat is a bear-case trigger.
Management transition: new CEO (Fred Lowery) with COO and CSO moving to advisory roles from 2026-10-30; execution of the value-creation plan changes hands.
Working-capital sign: the model charges 15% of revenue growth as cash consumed; distributors that grow faster consume more.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 61.95-92.18.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL company facts (CIK 0001000228): FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q (period ended 2026-06-27, filed 2026-08-04) for cash, debt, bank credit lines, NCI, shares, SBC, equity-award taxes, D&A, interest, taxes; research/HSIC/Reports/HSIC_Metrics.csv for the revenue / EBITDA / FCF history.
data_sources.qualitative: Q2 2026 earnings press release (8-K EX-99.1, 2026-08-04) for guidance, segment growth and buybacks; 8-K 2026-07-30 (leadership transition); 8-K 2026-09-22 (revolver amended to $1.25B, maturity Sept 2031); research/HSIC/info.json business summary. HSIC_Analysis.json did not exist at build time.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement via SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation $39M (operating add-back) + PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $15M (financing). Company publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $850M (PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock); H1 2026 a further $325M (4.2M shares at $77.05); $455M authorization remaining at 2026-06-27. FY2025 also saw a $250M primary issuance to KKR (ProceedsFromIssuanceOfCommonStock), a genuine non-SBC issuance already reflected in the share count and not repeated in the projection. The flat count is fully funded by the repurchase programme.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 111.92M shares outstanding at 2026-06-27 (Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, CommonStockSharesOutstanding) + 0.95M dilutive securities (Q2 2026 diluted WA 114.39M less basic WA 113.45M). Cover page shows 111.45M at 2026-07-27 after further buybacks, but the 6/27 count matches the balance-sheet cash used for net debt. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Last Saturday of December (FY2025 ended 27 Dec 2025)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-28T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 61.95-92.18
inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt $3,462M = LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations $2,300M + current maturities $138M + bank credit lines / ShortTermBorrowings $1,024M (all at 2026-06-27, Q2 2026 10-Q). NOTE: the Metrics.csv TotalDebt column (2,438) omits the $1,024M of bank credit lines. Cash $157M (CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents 2026-06-27). Net debt/GAAP EBITDA ~3.3x, ~2.9x on adjusted EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities ($351M) are NOT in net debt because the lease cost sits inside EBITDA (see lease_treatment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (senior notes + credit lines), after-tax ~3.85% at 23%. Capital structure ~74% equity ($9.7B market cap) / 26% debt ($3.5B) -> WACC ~7.4%, rounded to 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios; risk is charged through scenario weights, not per-scenario rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): US GAAP ASC 842 operating lease cost ($94M FY2025) is expensed inside operating income, so EBITDA is post-lease and operating lease liabilities ($351M) are excluded from net debt. Finance leases are immaterial ($6M) and sit inside reported debt. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0 -- charging it would double count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (revenue, EBITDA, capex include the majority-owned subsidiaries such as Henry Schein One and the specialty businesses), so NCI is deducted once, in the equity bridge, at $1,566M: MinorityInterest (permanent equity) $660M + TemporaryEquityCarryingAmount (redeemable NCI, carried at redemption value -- these are put obligations the company must fund) $906M, both at 2026-06-27. NCI share of FY2025 net income was only ~$16M ($21M permanent, -$5M redeemable), depressed by acquired-intangible amortization at the subsidiary level, so the balance-sheet deduction is the more honest measure of the claim.
inputs.ebitda_basis_note: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A + SBC add-back): FY2025 (653 + 311 + 39) / 13,184 = 7.61%; H1 2026 (353 + 165 + 16) / 6,826 = 7.82%. GAAP, not the company's Adjusted EBITDA (~$1.1B, ~8.4%), because restructuring / value-creation / cyber / litigation costs have recurred every year since 2022 and are real cash. The base margin expansion of ~90bp to 8.5% pre-SBC assumes the $75-100M value-creation savings partly drop through and restructuring tapers; the bull case reaches the adjusted-EBITDA level (~9.3% pre-SBC) as restructuring ends.
inputs.growth_note: FY2026 guidance (2026-08-04, raised): total sales growth 4.5-5.5%, of which ~0.7% acquisitions and ~1.5-2% FX are already in H1 actuals; internal growth 3.6% H1, 4.6% in Q2. Year 1 uses the 5.0% guidance midpoint; later years are organic only (3-4% base) and tuck-in acquisition spend (~$200M/yr, FY2025 $199M) is deliberately excluded from BOTH the growth path and the flows so the two are consistent.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company, dental/medical distributor + specialty products + practice software), first valuation of this ticker. Latest FCF is used as the anchor rather than a mid-cycle figure: FY2025 OCF $712M / FCF $573M is in line with FY2020-25 reported FCF of $506-700M and there is no commodity or cycle peak to normalize; the FY2023-24 dip was the October 2023 cyber incident, since recovered. Year-1 owner FCF from the component build (~$620M unlevered) is consistent with FY2025 owner FCF of $519M levered plus ~$115M after-tax interest. Working capital: distributor with receivables + inventory > payables (~19% of revenue), so growth consumes cash and wc_capture_pct is negative. D&A (2.36% of revenue) far exceeds capex (1.05%) because it carries $180M of acquired-intangible amortization; da_pct_path glides down to 1.3% as those intangibles roll off, since no new acquisitions are modelled. Cash tax rate 23% on unlevered EBIT (FY2025 GAAP effective ~22.5%, cash taxes paid $128M). Interest income ($33M FY2025, mostly customer financing) is left in the flows: the company carries net debt, so there is no cash pile being double counted. KKR took a ~12% stake in FY2025 (incl. $250M primary issuance) and the CEO changed to Fred Lowery; COO and CSO transition to advisory roles 2026-10-30 (8-K 2026-07-30). Revolver upsized to $1.25B and extended to Sept 2031 on 2026-09-21 (8-K 2026-09-22).

bear.narrative: H2 2026 holds near guidance (FX and closed acquisitions are already in the numbers) but organic growth then stalls at 1.5%: dental patient traffic stays soft, Amazon Business / direct-from-manufacturer channels take price on consumables, and equipment stays cyclical. Restructuring never ends and gross-margin pressure takes the pre-SBC margin down to 7.0%. Working capital drag at 18%. 14x terminal cap, 1.5% terminal growth. Not a solvency case -- the revolver runs to 2031 -- but with ~3x net debt/EBITDA and $906M of NCI puts, the equity absorbs all of the disappointment.

base.narrative: Guidance-midpoint FY2026 (+5.0% incl. FX and closed tuck-ins), then 3-4% organic: dental merchandise mid-single digit, equipment low-single digit, medical ~4%, technology high-single digit. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~90bp to 8.5% by FY2029 as value-creation savings ($75-100M) partly drop through and restructuring tapers; SBC flat at 0.41% of revenue; D&A glides down as acquired intangibles amortize out; capex 1.1%; working capital consumes 15% of each year's revenue increase. 16x terminal cap for a low-growth distributor.

bull.narrative: Top of guidance and a sustained dental-market recovery: specialty (implants, endo, ortho) and Henry Schein One software grow high-single digit and mix the group toward 5% for several years. Restructuring ends and the full value-creation programme drops through, lifting the pre-SBC margin to 9.3% (the company's adjusted-EBITDA level plus operating leverage). Tighter working capital (12% capture). 18x terminal cap, 3% terminal growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: net debt ~3x EBITDA (once the $1.0B of bank credit lines is counted), $906M of redeemable NCI puts ranking ahead of common, a low-single-digit organic growth business exposed to dental-visit cyclicality, and a margin thesis that depends on restructuring actually ending after four consecutive years of it. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (dental recovery, full value-creation drop-through, and specialty/software mix) and the company's own track record on margins since FY2021 is negative. Base 50%: guidance was raised in August and H1 2026 delivered, so the central case is well anchored.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
